title: Adjustable backoff presets, idempotency contract, and unified retryable-error catalog for cross-SDKs
creator: Aaron Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) currently have inconsistent retry/backoff defaults, idempotency key ergonomics, and different views of which errors are retryable across HTTP, gRPC, and streaming transports. This causes subtle production bugs: duplicate operations when idempotency is unclear, overly aggressive retries increasing cost and latency, and inconsistent developer expectations across languages.

Goal:
Define and implement a unified, configurable defaults surface for backoff profiles and retry policies across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs; specify a small, explicit idempotency contract and helpers for common ops; and publish a canonical retryable-error taxonomy that maps transport-level errors and server-side signals to SDK decisions. Provide ergonomic examples and migration guidance.

Non-goals:
- Replacing server-side error semantics (we will adapt SDK behavior to server signals).
- Exhaustive list of all possible platform errors — focus on common, high-impact categories.

Design proposal (summary):
1) Backoff profiles: introduce three named profiles: "fast-fail" (low retries, short jittered exponential up to 500ms), "balanced" (default; moderate retries, base 150ms, max 2s), and "throughput" (higher retries with longer caps to favor eventual success). Each profile is exposed as an immutable struct/class and a pluggable policy interface.
2) Retry policy DSL: SDKs will expose a RetryPolicy object with fields: max_attempts, initial_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, multiplier, jitter, retryable_error_set, and idempotency_mode_hint. Provide helpers to derive policies from the named profiles.
3) Idempotency contract: define two operation categories: "naturally-idempotent" (read, safe queries, stateless token requests) and "mutating-with-key" (create/update ops that accept explicit idempotency keys). SDKs will provide a consistent helper: generate_idempotency_key() and an optional auto-key feature that can be enabled per-client (off by default). Document semantics for streams: streaming append/update should surface a per-stream message id if server supports dedup.
4) Retryable-error taxonomy: canonical list (server HTTP + gRPC + transport): transient-network (connection reset, timeout), throttling (HTTP 429, gRPC RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED), server-transient (HTTP 502/503/504, gRPC UNAVAILABLE), client-misconfig (4xx non-retryable except 409/429), rate-limited-consistent (HTTP 409 with idempotency conflict -> do not retry unless idempotency key indicates safe retry). Special case: streaming errors with partial response must surface a resume token; retry logic for streams will prefer resume over full restart. Provide mapping table in docs.
5) Defaults and migration: default policy in each SDK = "balanced" with idempotency auto-key = false. Add opt-in environment variable/constructor flag to adopt "throughput" policy for workloads that prefer retries. Provide compatibility shim for existing users to retain previous behavior for a 1-release window.

Examples (what to implement in each SDK):
- Python: RetryPolicy dataclass, client constructor accepts "retry_profile='balanced'" or custom RetryPolicy, helper function generate_idempotency_key(), integration with requests/httpx and grpc interceptors. Include a simple decorator @redwood.retryable(idempotency_key_fn=...) for high-level convenience.
- TypeScript: RetryPolicy interface + builder, default policy export DEFAULT_RETRY_PROFILE, auto idempotency via client option { autoIdempotency: false }, builtin UUID generator for keys, streaming retry adapter that uses resume tokens when available.
- Go: RetryPolicy struct, functional options on client.NewClient(...), idempotency helper redwood.IdempotencyKey(), context metadata propagation for idempotency and resume tokens.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cross-language spec document published in SDK docs with mapping table and examples.
- Python/TS/Go SDKs contain corresponding RetryPolicy API and implement default "balanced" profile.
- Idempotency helper functions implemented and documented; auto-key disabled by default.
- Retryable-error taxonomy implemented in each SDK mapping for HTTP and gRPC codes.
- Unit and integration tests cover retry behavior, including jitter/backoff and idempotency key propagation.
- Perf benchmarks for default vs throughput profile show <10% median latency degradation for balanced compared to current baseline, and meaningful success-rate improvement for throughput profile in high transient error scenarios.

Implementation plan / milestones:
- 2026-03-02: Draft spec + initial internal design review (done).
- 2026-03-05 -> 03-12: Implement RetryPolicy surface + idempotency helper in Python.
- 2026-03-08 -> 03-18: Implement in TypeScript + streaming adapter.
- 2026-03-10 -> 03-20: Implement in Go.
- 2026-03-12 -> 03-22: Cross-SDK tests and perf runs; docs + migration guide.
- 2026-03-24: Release SDK patch releases; announce migration window and deprecation notices.

Open trade-offs / decisions needed:
- Auto idempotency: convenience vs accidental duplicate suppression for user intent. We default to off but we need legal/PM feedback for enterprise compliance (Sofia López requested additional review).
- Default retry counts: aggressive retries can hide flaps but increase tail latency for other customers — suggested tuned defaults above favor conservative balanced mode.
- Streaming resume tokens: requires server support; SDKs will expose resume-enabled adapters only if server advertises resume capability.

Telemetry and observability:
- SDKs should emit structured metrics: retry_attempts_total, retries_by_profile, idempotency_key_generated_total, resume_attempts_total, and events for retries that exhausted. These metrics will be mapped to Console dashboards.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for backoff math and jitter distribution.
- Integration tests using fault-injecting harness (local proxy that simulates 502, 429, timeouts) to validate policy behaviors.
- Streaming integration with simulated resume tokens and partial commits.
- Cross-language conformance tests that run same workload and validate identical observable behavior for a given policy.

Migration notes for users:
- Default remains conservative; opt-in path provided. When migrating to auto-idempotency, recommend using explicit idempotency keys for mutating operations and monitoring duplicates metric. Provide sample migration guide in docs and PR template for SDK changes.
